Boulder's iconic slanted sandstone formations, with 40+ miles of hiking trails accessible from the historic Chautauqua grounds; also popular for rock climbing.

National park in Colorado's Front Range covering over 415 square miles, with mountains, alpine lakes, large elk herds, over 300 miles of hiking trails and Trail Ridge Road, the park's main automobile route, built in the 1930s.
Narrow canyon south of Boulder with towering sandstone walls famous among rock climbers, plus creekside picnic areas and hiking trails.
Free weather and climate science exhibits in the I.M. Pei-designed National Center for Atmospheric Research building below the Flatirons, with a nature trail.
University of Colorado planetarium with full-dome science shows and an adjoining student observatory.
Free university natural history museum with dinosaur fossils, fossil-track exhibits and anthropology and zoology collections.
a.l: Henderson Building, 15th St & Broadway, Boulder, CO 80309

a.d: Scenic 48-mile highway through Rocky Mountain National Park between Estes Park and Grand Lake, reaching over 12,000 feet elevation; seasonal access only.
a.l: Rocky Mountain National Park, United States

a.d: Explore local highlights.
About one-mile wooden oceanfront boardwalk along the Atlantic, with Funland rides, summer concerts at the bandstand, beach access, and city public restroom facilities.
Delaware's largest water park: wave pool, lazy river, waterslides, spray ground, plus mini golf and batting cages next door.
37-acre public garden with a Piet Oudolf-designed meadow, woodland trails, and a folly garden; kids 16 and under get in free.
About 6.5 miles of ocean beach between Rehoboth and Indian River Bays, with swimming, surfing, fishing at the Indian River Inlet, and family camping.
Wooded 66-acre millpond with a water park, nature center, fishing, paddling, and campsites — an easy family day trip or overnight.
Three miles of quieter ocean beach with lifeguarded swimming, bay-side kayaking, paddleboarding, and crabbing.
Paddle among ancient baldcypress trees in the East Coast's northernmost cypress stand, with narrated pontoon tours, free bike rentals, and camping.
5,000+ acres of beach, dunes, and maritime forest with the Fort Miles WWII museum, Seaside Nature Center, and miles of paved bike trails.

Year-round, 17-mile ferry crossing of Delaware Bay between Lewes, Delaware, and Cape May, New Jersey, taking about 85 minutes. Open-air decks offer bay views and a chance to spot dolphins and lighthouses, and there is indoor seating with food and drinks.
Lewes museum in a 1931 building modeled on the town hall of Hoorn, Netherlands, covering Delaware's first Dutch settlement (1631) and local shipwrecks.
About 10,000 acres of marsh, ponds and woods along Delaware Bay, with walking trails, a boardwalk and paddling routes. Strong birding.
Rail trail of about 6 miles between Rehoboth Beach and Lewes, through woods, farm fields and salt marsh.
Campus of restored historic buildings in Lewes, the 'First Town in the First State', with tours and exhibits on the town's maritime past.
Busch Gardens Tampa Bay is a 335-acre animal theme park in Tampa with roller coasters, thrill rides, animal habitats and encounters, live entertainment, and kid-friendly attractions.
Large aquarium on the Tampa waterfront with a coral reef gallery, a wetlands trail under a glass dome and sea life of Florida.
Zoo in north Tampa with Florida manatees, African savanna animals, Asian and Australian sections and a manatee critical-care center.
Science museum in north Tampa with hands-on exhibits, a planetarium and science programs for children.
Children's museum in downtown Tampa's Curtis Hixon Park with interactive play spaces for kids up to about age ten.
Riverwalk history museum covering 12,000 years of Florida's Gulf Coast, including a full-size pirate ship and a cartography gallery.
Museum in a 1923 bakery building telling the story of Ybor City's cigar industry, with restored cigar workers' cottages (casitas).
County park on the Hillsborough River with a boardwalk through cypress swamp and an observation tower for spotting alligators and birds.
Day trip · about 25 km from Tampa. State park along the Hillsborough River with rare Class II rapids for Florida, a suspension bridge, nature trails and canoe rentals.
Day trip · about 35 km from Tampa. Marine rescue, rehabilitation and release aquarium in Clearwater, home to rescued dolphins, sea turtles and otters.
Day trip · about 45 km from Tampa. County park spread over five keys at the mouth of Tampa Bay with an 1898 coastal fort, nature trails, a fishing pier and kayak trails.
a.l: 3500 Pinellas Bayway S, Tierra Verde, FL 33715

a.d: Day trip · about 35 km from Tampa. Historic Greek-American sponge-diving harbor on the Anclote River where sponge boats still dock and sponge-diving boat trips leave.
Day trip · about 25 km from Tampa. Outdoor park with more than 150 life-size dinosaur models along shaded trails, plus a fossil dig and boneyard for kids.
a.l: 5145 Harvey Tew Rd, Plant City, FL 33565

a.d: Day trip · about 40 km from Tampa. Barrier-island state park off Dunedin with a nature trail through virgin slash pine, osprey nests and a ferry to Caladesi Island.
Explore local highlights.
The largest aquarium in the U.S., home to whale sharks, beluga whales, manta rays, and dolphin and sea lion presentations — a full-day family must-see.

Founded in 1889 in Grant Park, Zoo Atlanta is one of the oldest zoos in the U.S. It is a 40-acre zoo with over 1,000 animals from 200+ species, including giant pandas, elephants, and one of North America's largest populations of western lowland gorillas.
Interactive museum tracing Coca-Cola's history in Atlanta, with a 4-D theater, the Vault of the Secret Formula, and a tasting room where visitors can sample beverages from around the world.

a.n: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
a.d: Free NPS historical park featuring Dr. King's birth home, visitor-center exhibits ('Courage To Lead'), and The King Center along historic Auburn Avenue.
Dinosaurs, a giant-screen theater, and 75 acres of old-growth forest trails and outdoor WildWoods exhibits — Atlanta's science and nature experience.

Day trip · about 65 km from Atlanta. Smithsonian-affiliate science museum in Cartersville, about 45 minutes north of downtown Atlanta, with geology and fossil displays, the Bentley Planetarium, an observatory, and Fossil Dig and Gem Panning areas.

Day trip · about 90 km from Atlanta. A Georgia state park and lodge near Dawsonville featuring Amicalola Falls, hiking trails, mountain views, a restaurant, zip-lining, and activities like archery and hatchet throwing.

Preserves a 2,965-acre Civil War battleground of the 1864 Atlanta Campaign. The visitor center has a short film, a museum and artifacts, and the top of Kennesaw Mountain offers views of downtown Atlanta.
Day trip · about 120 km from Atlanta. Ancient Native American earthworks with a museum of 12,000 years of history, a reconstructed Earth Lodge, and eight miles of trails — free to enter.
3,200-acre park around the world's largest exposed granite, with a skyride to the summit, scenic railroad, family attractions, and the famous laser light show.

a.n: Roosevelt's Little White House State Historic Site
a.d: Day trip · about 100 km from Atlanta. FDR's preserved personal retreat, kept as he left it, with a museum featuring the Unfinished Portrait and his hand-controlled 1938 Ford convertible.
30-acre garden beside Piedmont Park with a tropical conservatory, an orchid house and the Kendeda Canopy Walk through the treetops.
Puppetry museum and theater in Midtown with live puppet shows for children, a Jim Henson collection and hands-on puppet workshops.
Day trip · about 25 km from Atlanta. National Park Service land along 48 miles of the Chattahoochee River with riverside trails, a waterfall at Vickery Creek and paddling.
a.l: 1978 Island Ford Pkwy, Sandy Springs, GA 30350

a.d: Hands-on play museum for young children next to Centennial Olympic Park, with exhibits on science, food and building.
a.l: 275 Centennial Olympic Park Dr NW, Atlanta, GA 30313

a.n: The Breman Museum (William Breman Jewish Heritage Museum)
a.d: Atlanta's Jewish history museum, with a Holocaust exhibition and the story of Jewish life in Atlanta and the South.
Aviation museum in Delta's original 1940s maintenance hangars at Atlanta's airport, with historic airliners including a Boeing 747 to walk through.
Day trip · about 30 km from Atlanta. 127-acre nature center in Roswell with river boardwalks through wetlands, woodland trails and rescued birds of prey.
Day trip · about 25 km from Atlanta. Protected granite monadnock east of Atlanta with rare rock-outcrop plants, nature trails, ranger-led mountain hikes and a treetop adventure course.
Day trip · about 25 km from Atlanta. State park west of Atlanta where a creek-side trail leads to the brick ruins of the New Manchester textile mill, burned in the Civil War.
a.l: 1750 Mount Vernon Rd, Lithia Springs, GA 30122

a.n: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum
a.d: Presidential museum of Jimmy Carter's life and term, with a full-scale Oval Office replica and Japanese-style gardens.
Day trip · about 110 km from Atlanta. Large garden resort in the Pine Mountain foothills with azalea trails, a butterfly conservatory, lakes and a birds-of-prey show.
An iconic, steep hiking trail climbing up the interior wall of a 300,000-year-old volcanic crater, leading to breathtaking panoramic views of Waikiki Beach and the Pacific Ocean.
A spectacular shield volcano towering 10,023 feet over Maui, offering a lunar-like red volcanic crater landscape and views that pierce through the surrounding clouds.
The "Grand Canyon of the Pacific," a 10-mile-long, 3,000-foot-deep gorge of red and green cliffs, seen from lookouts along a scenic mountain road.
Viewpoint at 4,000 feet atop Kōkeʻe State Park looking down the fluted green cliffs of Kalalau Valley to the Nā Pali coastline.
a.l: End of Kōkeʻe Rd (HI-550), Kōkeʻe State Park, HI 96796

a.d: Roadside double waterfall plunging about 80 feet into a pool, viewed from a lookout at the end of a short drive from Līhuʻe.
Lava-tube blowhole on the South Shore where surf shoots spray several stories high, often with a moaning roar.
a.l: Spouting Horn Park, Lāwaʻi Rd, Kōloa, HI 96756

a.n: Kīlauea Point National Wildlife Refuge & Lighthouse
a.d: Clifftop refuge on Kauai's northern tip with the 1913 Kīlauea Lighthouse and nesting seabirds such as albatross, boobies and nēnē geese.
Roadside overlook above the patchwork taro fields of Hanalei Valley and its wildlife refuge, framed by waterfall-streaked mountains.
a.l: Kūhiō Hwy (HI-56) near Princeville, Hanalei, HI 96714

a.d: Guided tours through a lush valley garden of the National Tropical Botanical Garden, with giant Moreton Bay fig roots, garden rooms and a secluded beach.
Seventeen miles of towering, knife-edged sea cliffs and valleys reachable only by sea, air or long trail; boat tours sail along it with sea caves and dolphins.
a.l: Tour departures from Port Allen, Kauai, HI 96705 (also Hanalei)

a.n: World Center for Birds of Prey
a.d: Live raptor demonstrations with eagles, falcons, and owls from The Peregrine Fund, the conservation group that helped save the peregrine falcon.
Compact, conservation-focused zoo where every admission helps protect endangered species, with giraffes, penguins, and a butterfly house.
Interactive, family-friendly museum exploring Idaho's history and culture, with exhibits on Native cultures, land, and people.

Billed as the Northwest's largest waterpark, Roaring Springs in Meridian, just west of Boise, has more than 20 water attractions, including a wave pool, family raft rides, an Endless River and the Bearfoot Bay kids play area.
Neoclassical capitol heated by geothermal water, with a marble rotunda and chambers open to visitors and self-guided tours.
Territorial prison operated from 1872 to 1973, now a state historic site where you walk through sandstone cell blocks, solitary cells and the gallows yard.
a.l: 2445 E Old Penitentiary Rd, Boise, ID 83712

a.d: More than 25 miles of tree-lined paved path along the Boise River linking parks, ponds and downtown, ideal for biking and walking.
a.l: Boise River Greenbelt, downtown Boise, ID 83702

a.d: Mesa above the Old Penitentiary reached by road or a steep trail, with panoramic views over Boise and the Treasure Valley, especially at sunset.
a.l: 3199 E Table Rock Rd, Boise, ID 83712

a.d: Historic Main Street in downtown Galena, lined with independently owned shops, restaurants, and 19th-century buildings.
The world's largest children's museum: five floors of hands-on exhibits including Dinosphere with dinosaur fossils, a carousel, and a planetarium.
See Indy 500-winning race cars, the Borg-Warner Trophy, and take a track tour around the famous 2.5-mile oval.
A triple-accredited zoo, aquarium, and botanical garden with an International Orangutan Center, dolphin shows, and animal feeding experiences.
Hands-on, family-focused museum of Indiana's natural and cultural history, in the heart of White River State Park downtown.
Interactive living-history park with a recreated 1830s village, costumed interpreters, a tethered balloon ride, and hands-on science areas.

Day trip · about 90 km from Indianapolis. State park near Marshall in western Indiana with deep sandstone ravines and scenic Sugar Creek. Trails range from easy walks to rugged ladder climbs, with a suspension bridge and steppingstones along Sugar Creek.
Downtown urban park on the White River with lawns, the Central Canal, river promenade and several museums plus the Indianapolis Zoo.
Three-mile loop along the downtown Central Canal with walking paths, bridges and pedal-boat and kayak rentals.

a.n: Garfield Park Conservatory and Sunken Garden
a.d: 1954 glass conservatory with tropical plants and a waterfall, next to formal 1916 sunken gardens with fountains in Garfield Park.
Eight-mile paved walking and biking trail linking downtown neighborhoods, the canal, museums and parks.
Museum of college sports in White River State Park with interactive exhibits and a 1930s-style basketball court.
One of the largest city parks in the US, with a reservoir, ornithology center, nature trails and boat rentals.
Limestone state capitol completed in 1888 with a stained-glass rotunda dome; free guided tours on weekdays.
Free guided and self-guided tours under the 23-karat gold-leaf dome of the Iowa State Capitol.
Iowa's only AZA-accredited zoo: giraffes you can feed, lions, tigers, sea lions, a Discovery Center, plus seasonal dinosaur exhibits.
Hands-on science museum in downtown Des Moines featuring interactive exhibits, live science programs, a planetarium, dome theater, and a Makers Studio where visitors can try experiments.

Free 4.4-acre downtown park in Western Gateway Park with more than 30 monumental sculptures by artists from around the world, all donated by John and Mary Pappajohn. Picnicking is allowed. Open sunrise to midnight.
Dome conservatory of tropical plants and orchids on the Des Moines River, with outdoor gardens including a water garden, plus hands-on kids' activities.
Theme park in Altoona, Iowa, near Des Moines, with over 100 rides including coasters like Tornado, plus the Adventure Bay water park.

Iowa State University's 17-acre public garden in Ames, featuring an indoor conservatory, a butterfly wing, and over 20 themed garden areas; named a Top 10 North American garden worth traveling for in 2023.

Heritage railroad running steam and diesel excursion trains through the Des Moines River Valley, crossing a high trestle bridge over Bass Point Creek. Operated by the Iowa Railroad Historical Society in Boone, Iowa.
500-acre outdoor museum walking through 300 years of Iowa: an Ioway Indian village, pioneer farm, frontier town, and 1900 horse-powered farm.
Six historic covered bridges on a free, self-guided scenic byway through rolling Madison County farmland, open year-round with no admission fee; you can walk through most of them.
Lake park near downtown with a two-mile loop trail and a lighted pedestrian bridge across the water, plus boat rentals in season.
Day trip · about 30 km from Des Moines. Restored tallgrass prairie refuge with a free-roaming bison and elk herd, an auto tour route and a prairie learning center.
Day trip · about 50 km from Des Moines. State park with 100-foot sandstone bluffs along Pease Creek and the Des Moines River, with stairs, trails and overlooks.
1920s English Tudor-style manor built with materials from England, open for tours with its historic rooms, library and gardens.
Kansas's top outdoor attraction, home to 3,000+ animals across themed habitats.

Open-air living-history museum recreating Wichita life in the late 1860s and 1870s, with 54 historic and recreated buildings on more than 20 acres, costumed history interpreters, a working blacksmith, and farm animals.
Hands-on science center on the Arkansas River with flight exhibits, a six-acre adventure playscape, and a domed theater.

a.n: Dwight D. Eisenhower Presidential Library, Museum & Boyhood Home
a.d: Day trip · about 140 km from Wichita. Presidential library and museum in Eisenhower's hometown, with family-friendly exhibits on WWII, the presidency, and his boyhood home.

Day trip · about 140 km from Wichita. Kansas state wildlife area in a 41,000-acre natural basin northeast of Great Bend. It is the largest marsh in the inland U.S. and one of the most important stopovers for migrating shorebirds in the Western Hemisphere.
Day trip · about 65 km from Wichita. Space museum and science education center featuring a planetarium, a two-story dome theater, interactive exhibits, and a re-created rocket lab.
Day trip · about 60 km from Wichita. Descend 650 feet into a working salt mine museum near Hutchinson, Kansas, with tram tours and mining exhibits.

Day trip · about 110 km from Wichita. Explore nearly 11,000 acres of preserved tallgrass prairie with a bison herd, hiking trails, and historic buildings including an 1881 ranch house and the Lower Fox Creek School.
Botanical garden with more than 30 themed gardens, including a children's garden, Japanese garden and butterfly house.
Aircraft museum in Wichita's 1935 Art Deco municipal air terminal, telling the story of the city as the 'Air Capital of the World'.
a.l: 3350 S George Washington Blvd, Wichita, KS 67210

a.d: Hands-on animal park west of Wichita where visitors can feed giraffes, lorikeets and stingrays and meet lemurs and big cats.
Watch Louisville Slugger bats being made on the factory tour, and hold authentic game-used bats from major league players in the museum.
The "State Zoo of Kentucky" with gorillas, tigers, polar bears, and a popular splash park for kids in summer.
Kentucky's largest hands-on science museum, with interactive exhibits, a four-story theater, and MakerPlace workshops for kids.
Day trip · about 150 km from Louisville. Celebrates America's sports car with 100+ historic Corvettes on display, hands-on exhibits, and the site of the famous 2014 Skydome sinkhole.
Day trip · about 120 km from Louisville. The world's longest known cave system with ranger-led tours for all ages, plus hiking, kayaking, and camping above ground.

a.n: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park
a.d: Day trip · about 80 km from Louisville. The log-cabin birthplace of President Lincoln enshrined in a neoclassical memorial, with a second unit at his boyhood Knob Creek farm.
85-acre riverfront park below downtown Louisville with lawns, playgrounds, fountains and walking paths along the Ohio River.
Former railroad truss bridge turned into a pedestrian and bike path across the Ohio River, linking Louisville's Waterfront Park with Jeffersonville, Indiana.

a.n: Falls of the Ohio State Park
a.d: Riverside park with 390-million-year-old Devonian fossil beds exposed along the Ohio River and an interpretive center, just across from Louisville.
Museum on Louisville's riverfront about the boxer Muhammad Ali, with interactive exhibits on his career and the civil rights era.
18th-century farm and Georgian brick house, a National Historic Landmark, with guided house tours and a visitor center museum.
389-acre Olmsted-designed park with rolling meadows, a 2.3-mile Scenic Loop for walkers and cars, and wooded hiking trails.
726-acre wooded Olmsted park on a hill south of downtown, with a summit overlook facing the city skyline and forest trails.
Beloved Uptown zoo with Louisiana swamp, African savanna, and Asian exhibits — a full-day family favorite.
Riverfront aquarium showcasing Gulf of Mexico marine life, with the Insectarium's butterflies and giant bugs in the same complex.
Guided daytime tours through the working float studios of Kern Studios, where artists and craftsmen build New Orleans' Mardi Gras parade floats.
A major New Orleans museum with immersive galleries, interactive experiences including a submarine exhibit and 4-D theater, suited for visitors of all ages.
2,800 acres on Lake Pontchartrain with 1829 sugar-mill ruins, the Tammany Trace bike trail, a sandy beach, and nature trails.
1,300-acre park with century-old live oaks, lagoons, a miniature train, the Carousel Gardens amusement park and Storyland playground.
10-acre garden inside City Park with more than 2,000 plant varieties, a conservatory, a Japanese garden and a model train garden.
Children's museum on 8.5 acres in City Park with indoor exhibits on the Mississippi River and food, plus outdoor wetland and garden play areas.
a.l: 15 Henry Thomas Dr, New Orleans, LA 70124

a.d: 350-acre Uptown park with lagoons, huge live oaks, a 1.8-mile path, playgrounds and a bird rookery on Ochsner Island.
Museum in an 1823 French Quarter apothecary shop, showing the history of pharmacy and medicine with antique bottles, instruments and a courtyard garden.
Day trip · about 50 km from New Orleans. Narrated boat tours into the Honey Island Swamp, a protected Pearl River wilderness of cypress, bayous, alligators and wading birds.
Maine's largest art museum, with rotating exhibitions and family programs in the downtown arts district.
Hands-on exhibits, a climbing tower, and live children's theatre at Thompson's Point.

a.n: Portland Head Light and Fort Williams Park
a.d: Historic lighthouse (Maine's oldest) set within the 90-acre Fort Williams Park, which offers picnic areas, hiking trails, recreation areas, and a children's garden.
